newsitem.title: JORDAN: U.S.-Jordan to discuss stronger military ties.
newsitem.headline: U.S.-Jordan to discuss stronger military ties.

text.p: A U.S.-Jordanian military commission will discuss in Amman this week boosting defence ties and a programme of security assistance to the kingdom, the U.S. embassy said on Tuesday.
It said in a statement that the annual meeting of the joint commission would be held on Wednesday and Thursday.
The talks, which this year are held in Amman, will focus on "future joint military exercises, U.S. security assistance to Jordan and other issues of common interest", the embassy said.
The U.S. delegation, which has already arrived in Jordan, is headed by Fred Smith, the principal deputy assistant secretary of defense for international security affairs, it said.

The United States says it is helping revamp Jordan's armed forces in recognition of its new role in the Middle East after King Hussein signed a 1994 peace treaty with Israel and turned against his former ally Iraqi President Saddam Hussein.

Washington has since provided Jordan with a $300 million military aid package aimed at bolstering the ageing armed forces of an Arab ally. The centrepiece of the package is a squadron of 16 F-16 fighter bombers due to be delivered early next year.
Last November U.S. President Bill Clinton named Jordan a major non-NATO ally of the United States, entitling it to priority consideration for military aid and equipment.
